choices.why: No candidate is green velvet, so this one departs from the brief on color; the tufted Chesterfield with rolled arms and turned legs is still the most classic and elegant option, and its 236 cm width can anchor the fireplace group in this period room.
A pair of cream wingbacks with nailhead trim and dark legs gives a traditional fireside look and matches the Chesterfield's turned dark feet.
The Persian medallion rug in charcoal and cream is large enough for the whole seating group and echoes the dark mantel and the light upholstery.
This is the only true dark-wood option, and its espresso finish and trestle base suit the classic scheme at a good size for the space between sofa and hearth.
At 65x101 cm it is the largest framed mirror, so it holds its own over the tall chimney breast, and its warm wood frame ties in with the pine floor.
It is the only lamp with a fabric drum shade, and its turned, weathered stem fits the traditional style beside an armchair.

answer.why: Since no green velvet sofa is available, a soft palette of gray, cream and charcoal with dark wood accents sits calmly against the pale blue-green paneled walls and the dark mantel. The Chesterfield, wingbacks, Persian rug and turned-wood lamp together build a classic, elegant setting centered on the fireplace.
